llm.summary: The skill is a coherent persona and memory system, but it asks for broad local execution and persistent agent behavior with some unsafe shell patterns and automatic memory changes.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a coding or full tool profile with exec/read/write/edit/memory access, reads ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json for workspace/routing discovery, and offers approved edits to host-level OpenClaw config. This is powerful and only partly contained by prompt-level approval instructions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is mostly Markdown templates plus shell helpers. Basic install does not appear to auto-run scripts or cron jobs; setup actions are presented as agent-run tool steps with approval, and cron jobs are labeled opt-in.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells the agent to apply silent checks on every incoming message, reload SOUL.md/USER.md/MEMORY.md at session start, and periodically prune/archive memory. That is purpose-aligned, but broad enough to affect future unrelated sessions and workspace state.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It creates persistent identity, operating-rule, memory, heartbeat, and learning files, and optional scheduled OpenClaw cron jobs. The cron templates are clearly opt-in, but the persistent instruction and memory model is central and should be understood before use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is broad and the artifacts largely match it: persona setup, workspace templates, memory integration, heartbeat/status behavior, optional Discord routing, and optional cron templates are all described in SKILL.md and supporting files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a persistent persona/memory operating layer for an OpenClaw agent and are comfortable granting coding/full tools. Review every proposed exec command and host config edit carefully, especially workspace paths, sed personalization, ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json changes, and any cron job setup. Avoid storing sensitive personal data or secrets in the generated memory files.
llm.findings:
[T01] expected: The persistent SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md, session-start reads, and silent per-message checks are real and central to the persona OS design. They are disclosed, but still create a material review concern because they intentionally influence future agent behavior.
[T09] unexpected: The shell setup examples interpolate <WORKSPACE> into unquoted mkdir/cp/ls/find commands, while the resolver can return configuration-derived paths without validation. The sed/heredoc personalization guidance also relies on prose sanitization rather than deterministic safe APIs.
[TP4] expected: I do not accept the broad description-mismatch finding as stated. The SKILL.md description advertises the same major areas found in the artifact: setup, memory, heartbeat, Discord routing, commands, templates, and cron guidance.
[SDI-4] expected: The skill says workspace operations stay under <WORKSPACE>, but also documents opt-in reads and writes under ~/.openclaw for routing/tool-profile configuration. This is disclosed but should be clearer as host-level configuration access.
[RA2] expected: Cron templates and heartbeat behavior are persistent, but the cron files repeatedly state they are opt-in and not auto-installed. The remaining concern is the always-on persistent memory/instruction behavior, not hidden cron installation.
[P3] expected: TEAM-template.md includes example Discord message send/read commands for team routing. This is expected for the feature, and SECURITY-template.md says external actions and sensitive sharing require confirmation.
[PE3] expected: References to .env.local and credential strings are placeholders or audit regex patterns; scripts/security-audit.sh scans locally and does not transmit credentials.
[P5] expected: The flagged phrase in the Night Owl Creative example is an idiom about not dismissing ideas, not an instruction to harm anyone.
[AR1] expected: The flagged 'NEVER refuse' examples are persona-style anti-patterns about accommodating user needs, not a blanket instruction to comply with unsafe requests.
[AR2] expected: The 'without judgment' phrase in the coaching example concerns tone when reviewing broken commitments, not suppression of safety warnings.
[SSD-3] expected: The setup asks for name, nickname, role, and goal and writes them into persistent workspace files. This is expected for personalization but creates a privacy consideration.
